perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He knows Jonathan as his childhood friend/best friend, and he often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He has recently felt that Jonathan is hiding something important; this made him anxious and suspicious, so he arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront Jonathan.
- In that confrontation, Christian told Jonathan he felt something serious was being hidden. He heard Jonathan admit he was keeping something back: Jonathan is in trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help and said they could face it together. He heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to suspect the trouble might be criminal. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, that he might be involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decided to look into the matter discreetly to make sure Jonathan was safe. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan is being framed and that someone is trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this, said he had leads but was not yet sure who was responsible, and planned to gather evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later came to believe the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it, that it was someone they both know and trust, and that he planned to confront them and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned that the person is dangerous but said he trusted Christian to do what is right.
- The actual name/identity of the culprit is not stated in the provided dialogue, though Christian believes he has identified them.
